source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Diversified export footprint across South America, the Middle East and Europe enhances resilience amid shifting global trade dynamics; fully integrated 'chips-to-film' manufacturing model described as insurance when tariffs spike and supply chains fracture. No explicit 'China+1' framing found, but diversification-driven export growth narrative is present.

crude_exposure.evidence: Major raw materials are PTA & MEG, byproducts of crude oil; the PTA-MEG raw material complex together accounts for 55-65% of total production cost. Crude price volatility and INR movement drive raw material price swings, passed to customers with a 1-2 quarter lag.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Cost pass-through to customers with 1-2 quarter lag; long-term agreement on import parity pricing for main raw material supply.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (largely USD-denominated) account for ~77% of consolidated revenue in FY25; company relies on import-parity pricing agreements and lagged pass-through rather than formal financial hedges.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company reported to have no currency hedges or other long-term supply contracts against forex risk; separate energy price agreements exist for CY2024-CY2025.
inr_exposure.evidence: European subsidiaries (Italy, Germany) contribute the bulk of export/overseas revenue, e.g. Q4FY25 European business turnover of ~Rs 728 cr vs ~Rs 2,269 cr from Indian operations; company faces aluminium and energy price risk with no disclosed currency hedging program.

govt_capex.evidence: India's power infrastructure plans imply incremental transmission & distribution capex of roughly Rs 5-6 lakh crore over CY26-CY30, of which management indicated 20-25% flows to electrification products (switchgear, transformers, protection relays); data-centre orders represent an estimated 12-16% of ABB India's order backlog. Record order backlog of Rs 11,094 crore, up 17% YoY, reflects strong government/infrastructure capex-linked demand.

rural.evidence: Nestle India derives roughly 20-25% of sales from rural markets and is deepening rural/semi-urban distribution, having added ~5.2 lakh retail outlets across urban, semi-urban and rural markets since April 2023; management has identified rural/semi-urban as the next major growth engine.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company sources significant imported commodities (coffee, cocoa); recent commentary notes coffee prices trending lower and cocoa prices subdued on improved supply, but no specific USD-revenue or hedging percentage was disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestle India's CMD stated the company was planning to avail the government's PLI scheme for food processing to boost exports (reported by Business Standard); current-year AR confirmation of realized PLI revenue benefit not located.

rural.evidence: Tier-3/4 towns show higher CAGR within the network; company runs a rural outreach program (GraminFit) launched across seven states testing 110,000+ patients, and continues calibrated expansion into Tier-2/3 markets in North and East India. Exact FY24-25 rural/Tier-3+ revenue % was not confirmed (a third-party figure of 39% for Tier-3+ cities was found but attributed to FY26, not FY25, so it was excluded).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company offsets foreign currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign currency receivables, creating a natural hedge; monitors currency positions and may use financial instruments for residual risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue split: Domestic ₹3,660cr (46.4%), International ₹4,236cr (53.6%) comprising Emerging Markets ₹1,510cr (+27.9% YoY), Europe ₹1,474cr (+4.4% YoY), Canada ₹1,252cr (+35.7% YoY). No distinct US-market line was reported separately in the sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure was among 9 domestic pharmaceutical companies approved in Group B of the Government of India's PLI scheme for pharmaceuticals (alongside Biocon, MSN Labs, Wockhardt, Alembic, Macleods, Biological E, Natco, Strides).

govt_capex.evidence: Government customers contributed 59.5% of revenue mix (figure is from Q1 FY26 customer-mix disclosure, the most recent data point found; a precise full-year FY24-25 government-revenue % was not located, so treat as an approximate/adjacent-period proxy).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue contribution stood at ~9.0% (Q3 FY25 figure, used as closest available proxy for FY24-25 export/foreign-currency exposure).

pli_scheme.evidence: Netweb received its first claim under PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware, amounting to ₹59.4 million; company is also eligible under PLI 2.0 for networking and telecom products.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party CDMO-sector analysis states growth in India's CDMO sector is being driven by the China-Plus-One diversification trend, and identifies Divi's Laboratories (alongside Syngene, Piramal Pharma Solutions) as within the highest-capability tier of Indian API/CDMO players positioned to capture share shifting away from China. This is analyst commentary, not a confirmed direct quote from Divi's own MD&A, since the primary AR PDF could not be accessed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Operating margins compressed to ~32% (vs historical ~37-38%) partly due to elevated raw-material and freight costs; company relies on long-term contracts with built-in price-adjustment mechanisms with customers/suppliers to manage volatility, and is backward-integrating via the new Unit-3 Kakinada facility to improve supply-chain resilience.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (predominantly USD/EUR-denominated) contributed ~89% of FY24-25 consolidated revenue (total revenue ~₹9,712cr); Europe alone contributed ~₹3,036cr (~31% of total revenue), with Europe+US together forming ~74% of export revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's API operations (Bollaram, Visakhapatnam campuses) fall within the applicant pool/product scope of the government's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs/KSMs (₹6,940cr envelope), but no confirmed evidence was found that Divi's is an actual approved beneficiary or receives PLI payouts.

rural.evidence: "Despite subdued demand across urban and rural geographies, the company continued to make steady progress, with robust revenue and underlying volume growth and healthy levels of profitability" - management commentary; also noted cautious optimism on rural demand recovery aided by a good monsoon and increased construction activity. New paints venture (Haisha Paints) is specifically targeting rural/semi-urban markets in four states.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carries minimal debt (debt-to-equity ~1.5%, net cash positive with ~₹25.7bn cash vs ~₹1.4bn debt as of a recent quarter), suggesting limited floating-rate liability exposure, though no explicit floating-rate % was disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM (Vinyl Acetate Monomer), a crude-oil derivative, forms roughly 35-40% of Pidilite's overall raw material costs; VAM requirement is met largely via imports, and management has cited passing through only ~75% of raw material price increases to customers while targeting a 21-24% EBITDA margin band.

inr_exposure.evidence: International operations (exports plus overseas subsidiaries in UAE, Bangladesh, Egypt, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Kenya) contribute approximately 6.5-7.3% of total revenue (~₹647cr overseas-subsidiary revenue in FY25); company is also a large importer of VAM, creating additional two-way foreign-currency exposure not fully captured by the export figure alone.

rural.evidence: Two-wheeler sector growth momentum expected to be sustained by rural revival, further premiumisation, and continued launches (industry-level commentary, not a Eicher-specific disclosed rural revenue percentage).

govt_capex.evidence: VECV commercial vehicle growth described as driven by replacement demand, rural consumption, and infrastructure development (industry/analyst commentary, not a company-disclosed percentage).

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield exports and VECV/Volvo CKD-CBU imports create FX exposure; specific hedging policy and USD revenue percentage not confirmed from a primary source.

rural.evidence: IHCL expansion strategy includes Tier-2/3/4 Indian cities alongside international gateway cities as part of its 'Accelerate 2030' growth plan; no rural revenue percentage disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Sector outlook described as demand outpacing supply, with recovery of foreign tourist arrivals and steady momentum across leisure, social and MICE segments supporting IHCL's growth; no explicit government-capex linkage or percentage found.

china_plus_one.evidence: NFIL has gained from a trend of pharmaceutical/agrochemical corporations shifting some production to India rather than China; company also entered long-term supply contracts with South African miners for fluorspar, partially de-risking itself from China-sourced raw material.

crude_exposure.evidence: Rating commentary notes exposure to volatility in key raw material prices and risk of HCFC phase-out affecting refrigerant (HFC/HFO) revenues, partly offset by backward integration into hydrofluoric acid; not specifically a crude-oil-linked raw material.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export share of revenue was approximately 77% in Q4 FY25 (quarterly figure, not confirmed as full FY2024-25 disclosure), implying material USD exposure; specific hedging policy not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Aurobindo is pursuing vertical/backward integration (e.g., Penicillin-G and 7-ACA API capacity via subsidiary Lyfius Pharma) to reduce dependence on China-sourced APIs/intermediates, consistent with industry-wide 'China+1' and Atmanirbhar Bharat API sourcing shifts; not framed in the sources reviewed as a direct China+1 revenue-growth driver specific to Aurobindo.

inr_exposure.evidence: US market alone was described as accounting for 'nearly 40%' of annual sales (~Rs 14,816 crore) in FY25, with Europe (~Rs 8,356 crore) and Growth Markets (~9% of revenue) also USD/EUR-denominated; a third-party estimate (unverified, low-reliability source) suggested combined USD+EUR revenue exposure exceeding 70%. No confirmed hedging policy quote found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Aurobindo Pharma's applications (via subsidiary Lyfius Pharma) were approved under the government's PLI scheme for Penicillin-G (15,000 MT) and 7-ACA (2,000 MT) API production, with potential PLI disbursal up to Rs 3,600 crore over six years; Penicillin-G API has since been commercialised.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company describes a 'China+1' strategy that includes both diversifying away from China and partnering within China (JV with Jinnaite Machinery Co. Ltd for a China-based driveline manufacturing JV) to build a geographically diversified, vertically integrated presence across North America, Europe and Asia; order book (~Rs 23,700 crore, ~70% EV-programme driven) cited as reflecting this diversification.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first automotive component supplier in India to receive Auto PLI scheme certification, for its hub wheel drive motor used in electric two-wheelers; company had filed seven applications for different products under the scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst commentary on Alivus (formerly Glenmark Life Sciences) API/CDMO business notes: 'For CDMO and API players, the geopolitical realignment away from Chinese supply chains has moved from thesis to revenue line item,' with the company pivoting to complex APIs and expanding CDMO to capture this shift (CDMO revenue grew 18% YoY in the relevant period). Sourced from third-party analyst coverage, not confirmed directly from the AR MD&A text.

inr_exposure.evidence: Regulated markets including the US, Europe, Latin America and India together contributed about 80% of revenue, per company results commentary, implying meaningful non-INR revenue exposure, though an exact USD % and hedging policy were not located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company financial commentary indicates gross margin as a % of revenue declined ~140bps to 54.7% 'due to the absence of Production Linked Incentive (PLI) benefits,' implying the company was a PLI scheme beneficiary in a prior period whose incentive subsequently lapsed/reduced; EBITDA margin was maintained at ~30% without PLI benefits.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company risk disclosures cite 'raw material inflation and forex volatility' as primary risks, without quantifying crude-oil-linked raw material as a distinct % of costs.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedges combined with forex derivatives; treasury operations actively monitor exposures and adopt layered hedging strategies.
inr_exposure.evidence: Lupin operates in 100+ markets and is exposed to currency fluctuations, particularly USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR; natural hedges and forex derivatives are deployed, though extreme currency movements can still impact profitability. INR weakness aids exports but pressures imports.

china_plus_one.evidence: IGI's lab-grown diamond certification volumes are linked to India's growth as a global manufacturing hub for lab-grown diamonds (alongside China), with certification volumes up 17% YoY to 3.56 million reports, but this reflects India/China as dual manufacturing hubs rather than an explicit China+1 supply-chain-diversification narrative in the AR.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/outside-India operations (spanning the USA, China, Belgium, UAE, Egypt, Israel, Thailand, Hong Kong and Turkey) contributed about 26% of FY2024 revenue (₹2.73bn of ₹10.53bn total), implying some non-INR revenue exposure, but exact USD-denominated % and hedging policy were not confirmed.

rural.evidence: Company materials describe Titan's retail network as targeting 'both value and premium segments across urban and expanding rural India,' but no specific rural revenue % was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Jewellery international footprint (including Singapore, UAE/Sharjah, USA - Atlanta & Santa Clara) stood at 23 stores (21 Tanishq + 2 Mia) versus 350+ Tanishq stores across 200+ Indian cities, indicating international/USD revenue is a small share of the jewellery business, though not quantified.
